messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'mercuryfin-prod' (tenant: MercuryFin) reporting GPU utilization 98% and request queueing > 2 minutes. Impact: elevated latency/timeout for that tenant. Paging oncall-infra and oncall-ml. Link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/pools/mercuryfin-prod

ravi (oncall-infra): ack. I'm pulling scheduling/queue metrics now. Which models are spiking for them?

elena (oncall-ml): I'm looking at model telemetry — embeddings-worker-v2 and convo-large are both seeing long tail tokens. embedding requests are batched and holding. Could be a large backfill or customer job.

darren (eng-runtime): I see a sudden spike starting 06:12 UTC from a single tenant IP range. autoscale policy on that pool is {
  min_replicas: 2,
  max_replicas: 4,
  burst_allowed: false
}. KV cache memory is high; GPUs are saturated at 100% per-process. No recent deploys.

ops-bot: Recent events:
- 06:11:47 queue depth per model: embeddings-worker-v2=820, convo-large=120
- 06:12:03 avg token latency spike from 120ms -> 1.1s
- 06:12:10 tenant error rate (5xx) 0.8% (mainly queue timeouts)

ravi (oncall-infra): what are our mitigation levers? can we temporarily grant burst capacity to this pool while we coordinate with the customer?

elena (oncall-ml): options (short list):
1) enable short-term burst (add 4 GPUs) to reduce queueing quickly
2) route MercuryFin requests to quantized model variant `conv-large-q4` (lower perf but much lower GPU memory)
3) throttle/soft-rate-limit the tenant to protect other customers (policy: tenant_isolation=strong)
4) ask Accounts to approve emergency capacity (cost) so we can spin up Dedicated burst nodes.

darren (eng-runtime): technical constraints: pool is pinned to region uso-east-2, bursting requires infra approval and there is spare capacity in that region but it's on a per-tenant reserve. If we allocate burst we must set eviction_policy=tenant_isolation to avoid noisy neighbor. I can push the runtime change.

ravi (oncall-infra): ok let's perform a two-pronged mitigation: enable limited 30m burst (+4 GPUs) AND apply a temporary routing override to send MercuryFin embeddings to `embeddings-worker-v2-quant` while the burst ramps. I'll coordinate the commands.

sasha (accounts): pinged — I can approve up to 30m of emergency capacity for MercuryFin provided we capture the cost center. Confirm amount and duration.

support-liaison: drafting customer message. Will wait for confirmation of burst before sending. We should say: "We're seeing elevated queueing and are applying a short-term capacity increase and model routing to reduce impact. We'll follow up in 30 mins."

darren (eng-runtime): running grant command now:
```
rictl pools burst grant --pool mercuryfin-prod --gpus 4 --duration 30m --eviction-policy tenant_isolation --reason "emergency: queueing spike"
```

ops-bot: Burst allocation request received. Provisioning nodes...

ops-bot: Burst allocation complete. 4 GPUs added to mercuryfin-prod (instance ids: bc-11, bc-12, bc-13, bc-14). New pool capacity = 10 GPUs.

elena (oncall-ml): applying model routing override to route embeddings to quant variant for MercuryFin:
```
ri-api routes set --tenant MercuryFin --route embeddings --model embeddings-worker-v2-quant --priority 90 --duration 45m
```

ops-bot: Routing override accepted. Active routes for MercuryFin now include embeddings-worker-v2-quant.

ravi (oncall-infra): monitoring metrics. queue depth for embeddings dropped: 820 -> 110 within 90s. 5xx errors down to 0.05%. Latency stabilized ~180ms. Good.

sasha (accounts): approved per verbal with finance. Logging cost center: ENG-INCIDENT-2026-MERCURY.

support-liaison: sending update to MercuryFin (DM + status page): "we've added temporary capacity and routed embeddings to a lower-memory model to reduce latency. We're monitoring and will follow up with a detailed post-mortem if needed." :white_check_mark:

darren (eng-runtime): note: I set eviction policy so burst GPUs will drain any cross-tenant tasks first and preserve MercuryFin isolation. Also added a canary to detect if some internal batch job from the tenant is responsible. If it is, we should ask them to pause large backfills.

elena (oncall-ml): quick check: embeddings per-request token median down 65% for quant variant. Quality impact for their use-case should be minimal for now, but flagging for product to validate later.

ops-bot: Alert: scheduled auto-drain in 25m — burst to expire at 30m per request.

ravi (oncall-infra): handoff note for next oncall (Elena and Darren will remain looped): we've stabilized. Next steps: watch for re-spike, validate no cross-tenant degradation, request customer to defer large jobs. If queue depth > 300 again, escalate to infra lead for extended capacity.

elena (oncall-ml): copying to #postmortems and creating initial incident ticket (INC-2026-073-MERCURY) with timeline and metrics.

support-liaison: posted update to MercuryFin at 06:24 UTC. They replied: "Thanks, we're pausing our backfill and will confirm when done."

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Time to mitigate: ~6 minutes from page to reduced queueing. Follow-up owner: elena (oncall-ml).

ravi (oncall-infra): closing active paging. Leaving runbook note: consider enabling burst_allowed=true on this customer's autoscale policy if they have predictable backfills (requires account approval).

elena (oncall-ml): I'll own follow-up: validate model-quality delta, confirm customer paused job, and draft postmortem. Will update INC ticket by EOD.

ravi (oncall-infra): resolved_for_now :tada: — leaving monitoring for 2 hours and will re-open if metrics regress.
